rows.rationale: The two tests in tests/test_demo.py call pure functions directly with literal inputs and use no fixtures or factories. Assertions stay specific: an exact equality check for add and a ValueError expectation for a negative age. Pure tests like these need no factory.

No fixtures are declared or requested by the visible tests, and the module under test defines only two stateless functions with no module-level mutable state. No shared mutable state exists between tests in the supplied evidence. One excluded file was not available for review.

The test file imports only pytest and the demo package, and the demo package consists entirely of integer addition and integer parsing with no I/O. The project declaration lists no dependencies, so no database driver is declared. There is no database, server, or schema setup for these tests to reuse.

The tests and the complete module under test create no database identities, records, or namespaces. Both functions operate only on their arguments, so run or worker ownership of database records cannot arise in these tests.

No Redis, Valkey, or other cache client is imported by the tests or the demo package, and the project declares no dependencies. The code under test performs no caching, so there are no keys to namespace or clean.
Neither the tests nor the demo package write files or open listening sockets. Both functions are pure computations over their arguments, so temp-root and port ownership do not apply.

The tests import only pytest and the demo package, and the demo package contains no network client code. With no network targets in the code under test, there is nothing to deny or replace with a fake.

The tests and the demo package spawn no child processes. The runner configuration also declares a cooperative process group lifecycle for the runner itself, but the test code has no spawn or teardown paths to own.
The code under test reads no clock, sleeps, or uses threads or other synchronization. The tests assert on deterministic results of pure functions, so clock injection and barriers do not apply.

Test selection is disabled in the ptest configuration, with enabled set to false and closed_inputs set to false. Every run therefore covers the full suite, so there is no selective mapping that could need closed inputs or a full fallback.
The packet contains no ptest result or history timing data. Per-test durations cannot be judged from source alone, although both tests are pure computations with no setup cost.

limitations.message: One file in scope was excluded from the packet, so its contents, for example any shared fixtures, could not be assessed.
No authoritative python lockfile was admitted, so the provenance of locked dependencies is unknown.
Environments other than the reported project-local metadata were not inspected.
No per-test timing data was supplied in the packet.
This assessment is static and based only on the packet excerpts. The test suite was not run.
